discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors
motivation: The 2013 prize honoured the prediction of the Higgs mechanism; the experimental discovery that confirmed it remains unrecognized. Peter Jenni (founding ATLAS spokesperson), Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (founders and early spokespersons of CMS) conceived these general-purpose detectors in the late 1980s and led them through two decades of design and construction. Their choices, including high-resolution electromagnetic calorimetry, precision muon systems, and multi-level trigger architectures capable of selecting rare events at 40 MHz, made the 2012 observation in the diphoton and four-lepton channels possible. They opened a new experimental window: the direct study of the scalar sector, now yielding measurements of Higgs couplings to gauge bosons, third-generation fermions and muons. Their work set the model for large-collaboration science and the detector and trigger technology on which the field still builds.
